title: DP-KFC: Data-Free Preconditioning for Privacy-Preserving Deep Learning
claim: Standard private optimization collapses signal-to-noise in every layer; our data-free preconditioning restores it to match data-dependent preconditioners.
layout: 2 side-by-side bar-chart panels, shared bottom legend, log-scale y-axis per layer
description: Two side-by-side grouped bar charts share a log-scale y-axis labeled SNR. The left panel groups bars by layer (Conv1, Conv2, FC1, FC2) for a small CNN. The right panel groups bars by layer (L1 to L6) for a transformer. Each layer has three bars. Teal is DP-SGD, magenta is Public DP-KFC, and orange is Synthetic DP-KFC. The teal bars are very short, around 0.02 to 0.8, so the signal has collapsed. The magenta and orange bars are one to two orders of magnitude taller, and the orange bars are usually slightly taller than the magenta ones. The eye goes first to the gap between the short teal bars and the tall warm-colored bars. A single legend sits centered below both panels. The crop cuts off the top of the plots and the right edge of the right panel.
caption: Architectural Preconditioning. Comparison of Layer-wise Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) on (a) Simple CNN and (b) CrossViT-240 (Transformer) trained on CIFAR-100. Standard DP-SGD (Blue) suffers from signal collapse. DP-KFC reaches an optimal SNR profile across both local convolution and global attention architectures, matching the geometry of data-dependent proxies (Green) without accessing external data.
abstract: Differentially private optimization suffers from a fundamental geometric mismatch: deep networks have highly anisotropic loss landscapes, yet DP-SGD injects isotropic noise. Second-order preconditioning can resolve this, but estimating curvature typically requires private data (consuming privacy budget) or public data (introducing distribution shift). We show that the Fisher Information Matrix decouples into architectural sensitivity, recoverable via synthetic noise, and input correlations, approximable from modality-specific frequency statistics. We propose DP-KFC, which constructs KFAC preconditioners by probing networks with structured synthetic noise, requiring neither private nor public data. Empirically, DP-KFC consistently outperforms DP-SGD and adaptive baselines across diverse modalities in strong privacy regimes ($\varepsilon \leq 3$). DP-KFC matches private-data preconditioners while public-data variants degrade by up to $4.8\%$, showing that curvature can be estimated without consuming privacy budget or introducing distribution shift. This enables privacy-preserving learning in specialized domains (e.g., medical applications) where regulatory constraints make data scarce.
